title: Nasdaq Plummets 4% as Chip and Data‑Center Stocks Crash – Live Market Update
body:
U.S. equities plunged on Tuesday as the Nasdaq Composite slumped more than 4 percent, marking the steepest single‑day decline in the index since the early days of the pandemic. The sell‑off was led by a wave of profit‑taking in high‑growth technology stocks tied to artificial‑intelligence (AI) and data‑center services, sectors that had surged earlier in the year on hopes of a new wave of revenue. By the close, the Nasdaq was down 4.2 percent, while the broader S&P 500 fell 2.1 percent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 1.3 percent, signaling a broad‑based market correction.

The tumble was sparked by a confluence of factors that forced investors to reassess the lofty valuations that had been assigned to AI‑related companies. A series of disappointing earnings reports from chipmakers and cloud‑infrastructure providers revealed that demand for AI‑specific hardware and data‑center capacity, while still robust, was not expanding as rapidly as analysts had projected. In particular, several mid‑cap semiconductor firms disclosed weaker‑than‑expected orders for graphics processing units (GPUs) that power large language models, prompting a cascade of sell orders across the sector. The resulting price pressure spilled over into adjacent names, dragging down the Nasdaq’s heavy weighting in technology.

Market sentiment was further dampened by comments from industry insiders who warned that the AI rally may have been “a true panic” rather than a sustainable growth story. Jay Hatfield, chief executive of Infrastructure Capital, described the recent frenzy as a “classic case of investors chasing hype without solid fundamentals.” His remarks resonated with a growing cohort of analysts who argue that the AI narrative has become a catch‑all justification for inflated multiples, obscuring the underlying risk profile of many companies. As investors recalibrate, valuation gaps that had widened dramatically over the past six months are beginning to close, prompting a reallocation of capital toward more defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples.

The sell‑off also coincided with a tightening of monetary policy expectations. The Federal Reserve’s latest policy statement hinted at a possible acceleration of rate hikes to combat persistent inflation, a scenario that traditionally hurts growth‑oriented stocks. Higher borrowing costs raise the discount rate applied to future cash flows, which disproportionately impacts companies whose earnings are projected far into the future—precisely the case for many AI and cloud‑computing firms. Treasury yields rose modestly in the afternoon session, reinforcing the narrative that the macro environment is becoming less friendly to high‑growth equities.

Despite the sharp drop, some investors see opportunity in the volatility. Value‑focused funds have begun to increase exposure to beaten‑down semiconductor names, betting that the sector’s long‑term secular growth—driven by the proliferation of AI, 5G, and edge computing—will eventually outweigh short‑term headwinds. Moreover, analysts note that the broader market’s resilience, as reflected in the relatively modest declines of the Dow and S&P 500, suggests that the panic may be contained to the tech‑heavy Nasdaq. “We are witnessing a healthy market correction rather than a systemic crash,” said a senior portfolio manager at a major asset‑management firm, adding that liquidity remains ample and corporate balance sheets are generally strong.

Looking ahead, market participants will watch closely for the next wave of earnings reports, especially from the AI‑centric companies that have been the primary drivers of the rally. If those firms can demonstrate sustained revenue growth and clearer paths to profitability, the Nasdaq could quickly rebound. Conversely, continued disappointment or further indications of aggressive monetary tightening could extend the correction, potentially pulling the broader market into a more prolonged downturn. For now, the episode serves as a reminder that even the most compelling technological narratives must be underpinned by solid fundamentals and realistic growth expectations.
